findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the sentences about the unrelated audit, federal guidance, and coffee budget, or move them to a separate section. Keep this section focused on how the benefits team manages stipend coordination.
findings.violation: The section opens discussing benefits team coordination but then lists three completely unrelated topics (audit, federal guidance, coffee budget) with no connection, so a reader cannot name what the section is actually about.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Create separate sections for employee instructions and finance/payroll instructions, or use consistent second-person address throughout.
findings.violation: The passage shifts between employee audience (you record, you submit, you track) and implied finance audience (countersign) without clear boundary, so a reader cannot tell which instructions apply to them.

findings.evidence: The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year. [Later:] Employees keep proof of purchase for every stipend item. Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date.
findings.fix: Choose one term - either claim or request - and use it consistently throughout. Clarify whether proof of purchase and receipts refer to the same document.
findings.violation: The word claim appears once but is never used again; proof of purchase and receipts are used interchangeably without a stated equivalence.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year. The policy applies to one device per category per employee.
findings.fix: Name the real actor: finance team or the system moves the request; the company pays the stipend; you are limited to one device per category.
findings.location: How to Apply (line 21), Reimbursement Amounts (line 39), Restrictions and Exceptions (line 47)
findings.violation: Three sentences use abstract nouns (request, stipend, policy) as grammatical subjects instead of naming the actual people or organization performing the action.
